description:
What is in the sky over a location right now, from every satellite in the catalog (active satellites plus CelesTrak's visual group). For upcoming passes use find_best_pass or find_passes; for one satellite at any time, get_position with a place.

mode "visual" (default): sunlit satellites above minElevation while the sky is dark there (the Sun more than about 6 degrees down), brightest first; magnitudes are measured for most bright satellites (McCants' observations) and estimated for the rest. mode "radio": satellites with known downlinks above minElevation, day or night, those a hobby receiver can tune (30 MHz to 1 GHz) first, then the most recently heard by SatNOGS, then the highest.

Up to limit (default 10, up to 50). Satellites whose elements are more than 14 days from now are left out and counted. Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none. A heavy call: one at a time per caller; another waits up to 20 seconds, then is refused as busy.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

limit.description: how many satellites to return, 1 to 50. Default 10.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

minElevation.description: lowest elevation to list, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90). Default 10.

mode.description: "visual" (default): sunlit satellites in a dark sky, brightest first; "radio": satellites with known downlinks, day or night: those a hobby receiver can tune first, then the most recently heard, then the highest.
